## Findings

- **BERT-base — combined vs separate:** separate champions imply an expected combined-val accuracy of 52.9%; the combined-trained champion reaches 50.4% (-2.5 pts → combined training does not help).
- **DeBERTa-v3-base — combined vs separate:** separate champions imply an expected combined-val accuracy of 67.9%; the combined-trained champion reaches 70.0% (+2.1 pts → combined training helps). On test, that same combined champion decomposes to 75.0% easy (n=2376) / 56.1% challenge (n=1172).
- **DeBERTa-v3-base vs BERT-base on easy:** +17.9 pts, two-proportion p = 0.0000 (significant at 0.05).
- **DeBERTa-v3-base vs BERT-base on challenge:** +9.4 pts, two-proportion p = 0.0219 (significant at 0.05).
- **DeBERTa-v3-base vs BERT-base on combined:** +19.6 pts, two-proportion p = 0.0000 (significant at 0.05).

## Error analysis

Question categories are an automatic **lexical proxy** (regex over the question text), not the hand-labeled knowledge/reasoning taxonomy of Clark et al. (2018).

- **challenge/test — confidently wrong:** 87 predictions (7.4% of the set, 16.9% of all errors) are incorrect at confidence > 0.9.
- **challenge/test — position bias:** predicted position distribution ['23.9%', '27.4%', '24.7%', '24.1%'] vs gold ['22.7%', '26.5%', '26.5%', '24.3%']; largest deviation 1.8 pts → no meaningful answer-position prior.
- **easy/test — confidently wrong:** 104 predictions (4.4% of the set, 17.5% of all errors) are incorrect at confidence > 0.9.
- **easy/test — position bias:** predicted position distribution ['26.3%', '24.5%', '26.2%', '23.1%', '0.0%'] vs gold ['25.1%', '24.6%', '26.6%', '23.6%', '0.0%']; largest deviation 1.2 pts → no meaningful answer-position prior.
- **challenge — weakest question type:** *negation / except* scores 43.0% (n=79), -13.0 pts vs the subset overall, two-proportion p = 0.0158 (significant at 0.05).
- **easy — weakest question type:** *negation / except* scores 50.7% (n=73), -24.4 pts vs the subset overall, two-proportion p = 0.0000 (significant at 0.05).

## Still outstanding

- **No test numbers for BERT-base.** Its champion checkpoint has to be retrained before a cross-model *test* comparison (or any combined-vs-separate claim on test) is possible.
- All test cells come from a **single** checkpoint (the combined champion), while the validation cells come from three different per-subset champions — do not read a row as one model's profile.
- **BERT-base sweeps are single-seed**: gaps of ~±2 pts within a sweep are noise. Run the 3-seed final config before naming a champion in the paper.
- **DeBERTa-v3-base sweeps are single-seed**: gaps of ~±2 pts within a sweep are noise. Run the 3-seed final config before naming a champion in the paper.
